name: Pauri Bareli
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Gayki, G. M. 2023. Satpuda parisaratil vastavya aslelya Bhilala-Barela adivasi jamatichya lokgeetancha chikitsak abhyas [A critical study of the folk songs of the Bhilala-Barela tribe of the Satpuda region]. PhD thesis (Marathi), Sant Gadge Baba Amravati University. Shodhganga hdl 10603/516729.
sources.note: Contents page viewed (scan): seven chapters on folk-song genres, no chapter on the language; not downloaded further.

sources.citation: Maharashtra Sahitya Patrika no. 346, Oct-Dec 2013, pp. 11-12: review of Alka Kulkarni's novel 'Chakva' (Marathi), discussing Pawra-boli vocabulary used in the dialogue.
sources.note: Literary review; lists some Pawri words and Hindi loans; nothing phonological.

sources.citation: OLAC: 'OLAC resources in and about the Pauri Bareli language' (bfb), snapshot 2025-01-14.
sources.note: Lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue, Watters 2013 and Varkey & Vunnamatla 2018; no language description exists in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Varkey, Vinod Wilson & Kishore Kumar Vunnamatla. 2018. A Sociolinguistic Study of Bareli/Pauri and Related Languages. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2018-011. Dallas: SIL International. 197 pp.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (lexical similarity, RTT, Hindi SRT, questionnaires, 210-item wordlists in Appendix C for Pauri/Rathwi/Barli/Palya sites). No phonology chapter; the only occurrences of 'accent' are in the RPE proficiency descriptions ('heavy accent'). Silent on word stress. Sec. 1.3 lists prior work as TRTI Pune primers in Pauri, Sulya 1979 Bhilali Self-Instructor and Catholic religious materials only.

sources.citation: Watters, Stephen. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Bhils of Northern Dhule District. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2013-004. Dallas: SIL International (fieldwork 1987-88 among Paura, Vasava, Bhilori).
sources.note: Contents: lexical similarity, dialect intelligibility, bilingualism, language use; appendices of recorded texts and wordlists. No phonology; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Phillips, Maxwell P. 2012. Dialect Continuum in the Bhil Tribal Belt: Grammatical Aspects. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Pawri/Pauri/Bareli/Paura: no data on this language (covers Wagdi, Dehwali etc.). Nothing on Pauri stress.

sources.citation: Sarvekar, Kailas. 2012. 'Khandeshatil Leva ani adivasi boli' [The Leva and tribal dialects of Khandesh]. Bhasha ani Jivan (Marathi Abhyas Parishad, Pune) 30(4), Diwali 2012 'Boli visheshank', pp. 57-59 (Marathi).
sources.note: Only an outline of an MRSSM-funded research project whose planned ch. 7 is 'Adivasi Pawra boli: vyakaranik vaishishtye' (grammatical features of Pawra); gives the geographic spread of Pawra boli (Dhadgaon, Taloda, Akkalkuwa, Shahada, Shirpur, Chopda, Raver) but no linguistic data. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX, Part III: The Bhil languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia &c. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'Pawri' (Khandesh: Akrani/Dhadgaon, Taloda, Shahada), pp. 72-74 + two specimens.
sources.note: 'Pronunciation' paragraph covers a pronounced as broad a, o~u interchange, nasalized vowels, loss of initial h and of aspiration, chh pronounced s, s>h, pleonastic suffix -lo; nothing on accent or stress. The whole volume contains no accent statement for any Bhil dialect (only the transliteration note on the acute accent in the front matter).

sources.citation: Devy, G. N. & Arun Jakhade (eds.). 2013/2017. People's Linguistic Survey of India, Maharashtra volume (Marathi: 'Maharashtrachya bhasha', Padmagandha 2013; English: The Languages of Maharashtra, PLSI vol. 17, Orient BlackSwan 2017), chapter 'Pawari/Pavri'.

sources.note: The only dedicated grammatical handbook of Pavra (=Pawri/Pauri Bareli) ever published; Grierson's Pawri notes rely on it. Short, but the one place an early remark on accent could exist. Held at John Rylands (R 41268) and India Office collections; no scan located.
